title: ORCA Computing Launches PT-3 Photonic Quantum System in London for Hybrid AI and Industrial Optimization - Quantum Computing Report
gist: ORCA Computing launched PT-3, a room-temperature photonic system with 64 photons across 128 qumodes, first deployed at Digital Realty Innovation Lab in London alongside NVIDIA GPUs, with reported 20% protein-designability improvement and a 12x speedup over PT-2 on a 25,755-variable energy scheduling benchmark.

insights.claim: ORCA's third-generation PT-3 uses 64 photons across 128 qumodes, operates at room temperature, consumes 6 kW across two standard data center racks, and is field-upgradeable, with the first system deployed at Digital Realty Innovation Lab in London.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Low power and standard racks support the data-center deployment case for photonic quantum.

insights.claim: Paired with 32 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, PT-3 extended NVIDIA's Proteina model and improved the useful protein designability ratio by 20% over classical baselines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Vendor-reported; a hybrid-AI use case to watch for independent validation.

insights.claim: With JIJ's hybrid solver, PT-3 solved a 25,755-variable unit commitment energy scheduling problem, developed with bp and the UK NQCC, in about one hour, a 12x speedup over PT-2 with quality competitive with commercial solvers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Energy optimization is the industrial target; vendor-reported comparison against its own predecessor.
